list.title: Merchants
list.description: Wholesale resellers: USD deposit, status and top-up history.

detail.freezeConfirmBody: “{title}” will not be able to place new orders. Deposits can still be credited while frozen.
detail.unfreezeConfirmBody: “{title}” will be able to place orders again.

credit.title: Credit the deposit
credit.hint: Booked on the ledger as a posting pair: D merchant_deposit / C house_payments_received.
credit.orderHint: (optional; OUR order id — the UUID from orders.id, not the reseller's merchant_order_id)
credit.replayMismatch: Credited {booked} via a previously used key — the entered amount {typed} was NOT applied. Check the history below and submit the form again if a new credit is needed.
credit.amountInvalid: Amount must be a positive USD number with at most two decimals.
credit.orderInvalid: The order id is a UUID from orders.id. This looks like the reseller's merchant_order_id: the server would answer “order not found”, and that is the wrong place to look.
credit.confirmBodyOrder: The credit will be booked against order {order}: the amount lands in that order's refunded_usd. The attribution cannot be changed afterwards.
credit.replayOrderMismatch: The previously used key is booked against order {booked}, not the entered {typed}. An attribution cannot be re-pointed — check the history below.

debit.title: Debit the deposit
debit.hint: Posted to the ledger as C merchant_deposit / D house_payments_received. Not attributed to an order.
debit.reasonHint: (required; internal only, recorded on the deposit history)
debit.confirmBody: {amount} will be taken off «{title}»'s deposit, leaving {rest}.
debit.replayMismatch: {booked} was debited under a previously used key — the amount you typed, {typed}, was not applied. Check the history below.
debit.amountInvalid: Amount must be a positive USD value with at most two decimals.
debit.reasonRequired: A debit needs a reason: it is the only record of why the balance fell.
debit.overdraw: Cannot debit more than the balance, which is {balance}.
debit.noWebhook: The merchant is not notified — there is no balance.debited event. They will see the movement on their statement.

keys.title: API keys
keys.hint: The merchant's server needs a key for /merchant/v1. The secret is shown once, at issue. Several keys may be live at a time so rotation has no downtime.
keys.empty: No keys — this merchant cannot reach the API
keys.ipHint: (one per line; empty means no restriction; cannot be changed on an issued key)
keys.secretBody: Hand both values to the merchant, then close this panel. We keep it encrypted and cannot show it again.
keys.keyIdHint: Public, starts with ypm_. This is what goes in the X-Merchant-Key header.
keys.secretHint: Starts with ypms_. The request is signed with it; it is never sent in a header. Not the webhook secret — that one starts with ypmw_.
keys.secretReplayed: This key was already issued under the same idempotency key, so the response carries no secret. Revoke it and issue a new one.
keys.saved: I have passed the secret on
keys.revokeConfirmBody: Requests signed with {key} stop working immediately. This cannot be undone — if the merchant still needs access, issue a new key.

hook.title: Webhook
hook.hint: Where we send order.status_changed and balance.credited. The voucher code is not in the body — only the order read hands that over.
hook.none: No webhook configured — the merchant learns about delivery only by polling
hook.reenableNote: Saving the URL also turns the webhook back on and resets the failure counter. The secret does not change.
hook.secretTitle: The signing secret is shown once
hook.secretBody: Hand it to the merchant, then close this panel. We keep it encrypted.
hook.secretNull: The secret did not change — the URL was updated and the existing signature still works.
hook.saved: I have passed the secret on
hook.rotateConfirmBody: The old secret stops signing immediately — there is no overlap window. Every delivery fails until the merchant updates their verifier.
hook.disableConfirmBody: Deliveries stop. The URL and the log are kept — saving the URL again turns it back on.

users.title: Cabinet operators
users.hint: Who can sign into this merchant's cabinet. “I cannot log in” is usually an unconfirmed address rather than a password.
users.empty: No operators — nobody has opened the cabinet; the account was created by hand

log.title: Delivery log
log.hint: The same one the merchant sees. When they say nothing is arriving, the answer is here.

markup.title: Per-merchant markup
markup.hint: Percentage points added to every SKU's own markup for this merchant. The catalogue usually sits at 7%, so −2 prices them at 5% over cost, on everything at once. Negative is a discount.
markup.none: Now: the catalogue price, like everyone else
markup.label: Markup, pp
markup.invalid: The markup is a number in percentage points, at most two decimals.
markup.floorError: That is too low: the thinnest SKU in the catalogue carries {thinnest} pp and the margin floor is {floor}%. The lowest that works here is {lowest} pp.
markup.confirmBody: It takes effect immediately and across the whole catalogue: {title} will buy at {value} pp against the base markup. Orders already placed do not change.

sku.title: B2B (merchants)
sku.visibleHint: The SKU shows in the B2B catalog only if B2B is also enabled on its brand.
sku.markupInvalid: Markup must be a number up to ±999.99 with at most two decimals.
sku.previewBelowCost: below cost — check the markup sign
sku.previewNoCost: Without a USDT cost the SKU has no B2B price — it will not appear in the merchant catalog.

brand.title: B2B (merchants)
brand.visibleHint: Off — the whole brand is hidden from the B2B catalog regardless of its SKUs' settings.

bulk.markupInvalid: Markup must be a number up to ±999.99 with at most two decimals.
bulk.action: Set markup on all brand SKUs
bulk.confirmTitle: Apply the markup to every SKU of this brand?
bulk.confirmBody: Every SKU of “{brand}” will get a B2B markup of {markup}%. Current per-SKU values will be overwritten.

settle.title: Merchant deposit
settle.confirmTitle: Return the money to the deposit?
settle.confirmBody: {amount} goes back to «{merchant}»'s deposit for order {order}.
settle.confirmClosing: The order will be closed as failed: once the whole charge is back it cannot be delivered — retry and manual delivery both refuse it.
settle.note: Settlement for order {order}, from the order page
settle.alreadySettled: This order has already had its money returned — it cannot happen twice. See «Returned» above and the merchant's deposit history.

blocked.no_charge: This order has no deposit charge — there is nothing to return.
blocked.partly_settled: Part of it is already back. Finish the rest on the merchant's page, where you type the amount.
blocked.settled: Fully returned — the order is closed and there is nothing to do.
blocked.still_open: The order has not ended yet — there is nothing to return until the delivery has terminally failed.

list.title: Blog
list.description: Guides and news bound to a catalogue brand.

form.coverHint: PNG / JPEG / WebP, up to 5 MB. Uploaded to cdn.yupay.uz.
form.editorPlaceholder: Write, then select text and tap a heading, list, or link.
form.pinCount: Other published pins on this brand: {used} of {cap}.
form.pinCap: Cap reached. Unpin another published post or publish will fail.
form.eventHint: Local time. The API stores UTC.
form.eventNeedWindow: Start and end are required, and end must be later.
form.eventLive: Live — the storefront will show a «now» chip.
form.eventEnded: Over — the post stays as history.
form.faqHint: The same copy is shown on the page and emitted as FAQPage JSON-LD.
form.faqEmpty: No FAQ yet. A guide usually wants 2–4 short questions.
form.faqIncomplete: Each pair needs both a question and an answer.
form.needSchedule: Pick a publish time in the future.
form.title: Title (H1)
form.needTranslation: At least one locale needs a title and a slug.
form.brandDraftHint: A draft can be saved without a brand. Publishing requires one.
